uncited: This family encompasses compression techniques that exploit specific hardware capabilities or data format constraints rather than general statistical redundancy.
It addresses the problem of memory bandwidth and storage inefficiency by mapping volumetric data into formats natively supported by GPU architectures or specialized hardware accelerators.

Unlike general-purpose methods like [Arithmetic Encoding](2127-arithmetic-encoding.md) or [Wavelet and Transform-based Compression](6879-wavelet-and-transform-based-compression.md), these methods prioritize decoding speed and hardware compatibility, often at the cost of flexibility or compression ratio.

They are distinct from [Sparse structures](5-sparse-structures.md) which rely on spatial sparsity, and from [Deferred Filtering Architecture for Compressed Volumes](857-deferred-filtering-architecture-for-compressed-volumes.md) which focuses on rendering pipeline integration.
The children in this family share no common algorithmic mechanism beyond the general principles of [Compression](4-compression.md).
They differ fundamentally in their target domain (frequency vs. spatial, spectral vs. color) and their reliance on specific hardware formats.

This variant packs three time steps of volumetric data into the Red, Green, and Blue channels of a 3D texture, then applies standard Video Texture Compression (VTC) algorithms designed for 3D-RGB data.
This approach exploits temporal redundancy by treating time as a spatial dimension, leveraging hardware-accelerated VTC decoders.
The need for hardware-specific compression arises from the bottleneck between GPU memory and processing units.

The 16-bit floating point format for spectra addresses the precision requirements of frequency-domain rendering, while RGBA packing addresses the bandwidth needs of color data in spatial-domain rendering.
